description: Dr. Yashwant Singh Parmar was a distinguished leader and the first Chief Minister of Himachal Pradesh, widely regarded as the architect of the state.

name: Freedom Forty - Swaraj
description: Issued to commemorate the 40th anniversary of India's independence, this stamp celebrates the concept of 'Swaraj' (self-rule) and the nation's freedom struggle.

name: Durgadas Rathore
description: Veer Durgadas Rathore was a legendary 17th-century Rajput warrior who preserved the independence of Marwar against Mughal forces.

name: Sarat Chandra Bose
description: Sarat Chandra Bose was a leading Indian independence activist, barrister, and the elder brother of Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose.

name: Gopinath Kaviraj
description: Gopinath Kaviraj was a renowned Sanskrit scholar, Indologist, and philosopher who served as the principal of Government Sanskrit College, Varanasi.

name: Hindi Day
description: Commemorating Hindi Day (Hindi Diwas), celebrated annually on September 14 to mark the adoption of Hindi in the Devanagari script as an official language of India.

name: Sports: Indian Olympic Association
description: Issued to honor the Indian Olympic Association (IOA), the governing body responsible for selecting athletes to represent India at the Olympic Games.

name: Sports: Freedom Forty - Glory of Sport
description: Part of the 'Freedom Forty' series, this stamp celebrates India's achievements and progress in the field of sports over forty years of independence.

name: Baba Kharak Singh
description: Baba Kharak Singh was a prominent Sikh political leader, freedom fighter, and the first president of the Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee (SGPC).

name: Jerdon's Courser
description: A stamp highlighting the Jerdon's Courser, an extremely rare and critically endangered nocturnal bird endemic to Andhra Pradesh, India.

name: Bangalore G. P. O.
description: Commemorating the General Post Office (GPO) of Bangalore, a landmark heritage building and a vital hub of postal services in Karnataka.

name: Bombay G. P. O.
description: Celebrating the Mumbai General Post Office (GPO), an architectural masterpiece built in the Indo-Saracenic style, which is one of the largest post offices in the world.

name: The Times of India
description: Issued to mark the 150th anniversary (sesquicentennial) of The Times of India, one of India's oldest and most widely circulated English-language daily newspapers.

name: Maulana Abul Kalam Azad Centenary 1888-1988
description: Commemorating the birth centenary of Maulana Abul Kalam Azad, a towering freedom fighter, Islamic scholar, and the first Education Minister of independent India.

name: Jawaharlal Nehru Centenary
description: Issued to mark the birth centenary celebrations of Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru, the first Prime Minister of independent India and a key architect of the modern nation.

name: Jawaharlal Nehru Centenary: Jawaharlal Nehru
description: A special commemorative stamp depicting Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru, issued as part of his birth centenary celebrations to honor his legacy and leadership.

name: Birsa Munda
description: Birsa Munda was a charismatic tribal freedom fighter, religious leader, and folk hero who spearheaded the Millenarian movement against British colonial rule in the late 19th century.

name: Sheikh Mohammed Abdullah
description: Known as 'Sher-e-Kashmir' (Lion of Kashmir), Sheikh Mohammed Abdullah was a prominent leader of Jammu & Kashmir and served as its Prime Minister and Chief Minister.

name: Bhakra Dam 1963-1988
description: Commemorating the 25th anniversary of the dedication of the Bhakra Dam to the nation, a monumental engineering feat described by Nehru as a 'Temple of Resurgent India.'

name: World Philatelic Exhibition: Early D. L. O. Cancellation
description: Issued in anticipation of the India '89 World Philatelic Exhibition, depicting an early Dead Letter Office (D.L.O.) cancellation mark from Indian postal history.

name: World Philatelic Exhibition: Early R. M. S. Cancellation
description: Issued for the India '89 World Philatelic Exhibition, showcasing an early Railway Mail Service (R.M.S.) cancellation mark used in colonial India.

name: K. M. Munshi
description: Kanhaiyalal Maneklal Munshi was an eminent freedom fighter, politician, writer, and the founder of the Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan.

name: Hare Krushna Mahtab
description: Dr. Harekrushna Mahtab, known as 'Utkal Keshari', was a prominent freedom fighter, leader of the Indian National Congress, and the first Chief Minister of Odisha.

name: Mannathu Padmanabhan
description: Mannathu Padmanabhan was a pioneering social reformer and freedom fighter from Kerala, best known as the founder of the Nair Service Society (NSS).

name: Lok Sabha Secretariat
description: Commemorating the Lok Sabha Secretariat, the independent body that provides administrative and procedural support to the lower house of the Parliament of India.

name: State Museum, Lucknow
description: Celebrating the State Museum in Lucknow, one of the oldest and most prestigious museums in Uttar Pradesh, housing a rich collection of archaeological and historical artifacts.

name: Baldev Ramji Mirdha 1889-1956
description: Baldev Ram Mirdha was an influential social reformer, farmer leader, and freedom fighter from Rajasthan who worked extensively for the upliftment of the peasantry.

name: World Philatelic Exhibition: Stamp Collecting
description: Issued for the India '89 World Philatelic Exhibition, promoting the hobby of philately and the joy of stamp collecting.

name: World Philatelic Exhibition: Traveller's Coach Post Office
description: Released for the India '89 World Philatelic Exhibition, depicting a historical traveler's coach post office used for mail transit in early India.

name: World Philatelic Exhibition: Travancore Anchel
description: Issued for the India '89 World Philatelic Exhibition, highlighting the 'Anchel' system, the historic postal service of the Kingdom of Travancore.

name: World Philatelic Exhibition: Earliest Philatelic Magazines
description: Released for the India '89 World Philatelic Exhibition, commemorating the earliest philatelic journals and publications that helped popularize stamp collecting.

name: Don Bosco
description: Commemorating Saint John Bosco (Don Bosco), an Italian Roman Catholic priest and educator who dedicated his life to the betterment and education of disadvantaged youth.

name: 3rd Cavalry
description: Honoring the 3rd Cavalry, one of the oldest and most decorated armored regiments of the Indian Army, with a rich history of valor and service.

name: Darga Sharif, Ajmer
description: Celebrating the historic Dargah Sharif of Ajmer, the revered Sufi shrine of Saint Moinuddin Chishti, symbolizing communal harmony and spiritual devotion.

name: President's Review of the Fleet
description: Commemorating the President's Fleet Review, a prestigious ceremonial event where the President of India, as Supreme Commander of the Armed Forces, reviews the Indian Navy.

name: B. G. Kher
description: Balasaheb Gangadhar Kher was a distinguished freedom fighter and the first Chief Minister of the Bombay State. He was honored with the Padma Vibhushan in 1954 for his contributions to public affairs.

name: Shaheed Laxman Nayak
description: Laxman Nayak was a prominent tribal civil rights activist and freedom fighter from Odisha. He led the Quit India Movement in the Koraput region and was executed by the British administration.

name: Rao Gopal Singh
description: Rao Gopal Singh of Kharwa was a revolutionary freedom fighter from Rajasthan. He is remembered for organizing an armed rebellion against British rule alongside Rash Behari Bose.

name: Rajkumari Amrit Kaur
description: Rajkumari Amrit Kaur was an eminent freedom fighter, social reformer, and the first Health Minister of independent India. She played a pivotal role in establishing the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS).

name: S. D. Kitchlew
description: Dr. Saifuddin Kitchlew was a prominent Indian freedom fighter, nationalist leader, and peace activist. His arrest in 1919 triggered the public protests that led to the tragic Jallianwala Bagh massacre.

name: Sydenham College, Bombay
description: Established in 1913, Sydenham College of Commerce and Economics in Mumbai is the oldest institution for commerce education in Asia. This stamp commemorates its platinum jubilee.

name: Bishnu Ram Medhi
description: Bishnuram Medhi was a prominent freedom fighter and the second Chief Minister of Assam. He also served as the Governor of Madras State from 1958 to 1964.

name: Asaf Ali
description: Asaf Ali was an Indian independence fighter, noted lawyer, and diplomat. He served as the first Indian Ambassador to the United States and later as the Governor of Odisha.

name: Dr. N. S. Haridkar
description: Dr. Narayan Subbarao Hardikar was a freedom fighter and the founder of the Congress Seva Dal. He dedicated his life to organizing voluntary service and promoting national integration.

name: Sankaracharya
description: Adi Sankaracharya was an 8th-century philosopher and theologian who consolidated the doctrine of Advaita Vedanta. He established four major monasteries (mathas) across the Indian subcontinent to unify Hindu philosophy.

name: Punjab University, Chandigarh
description: Panjab University is one of the oldest universities in India, originally established in 1882 at Lahore and later relocated to Chandigarh after the partition. It has been a premier center for higher education and research.

name: 75 Years of Indian Cinema
description: This stamp commemorates the platinum jubilee of Indian Cinema, celebrating its rich history, cultural impact, and artistic evolution since the release of Raja Harishchandra in 1913.

name: Kirloskar Centenary
description: Commemorating the centenary of the Kirloskar Group, one of India's pioneering industrial conglomerates. Founded by Laxmanrao Kirloskar in 1888, it played a vital role in India's industrialization.

name: D. A. V. Centenary
description: Celebrating 100 years of the Dayanand Anglo-Vedic (DAV) College Trust and Management Society. Founded in 1886, the society has established a vast network of educational institutions blending Vedic values with modern science.

name: Dakshin Gangotri Post Office
description: Commemorating the establishment of India's first post office in Antarctica at the Dakshin Gangotri research station. This unique post office was set up during the third Indian Expedition to Antarctica.

name: 125th Anniversary of Allahabad Bank
description: Commemorating the 125th anniversary of Allahabad Bank, which was founded in 1865. It holds the distinction of being one of the oldest joint-stock banks in India.

name: Central Reserve Police Force 1939-1989
description: Commemorating the 50th anniversary of the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF), India's largest Central Armed Police Force. Originally raised as the Crown Representative's Police in 1939, it was renamed after independence.

name: Military Farms Centenary 1889-1989
description: Celebrating 100 years of the Military Farms of the Indian Army, which were established to supply hygienic dairy products to troops stationed across the country. The first military farm was set up in Allahabad in 1889.

name: Mustafa Kernal Ataturk
description: Mustafa Kemal Atatürk was a Turkish field marshal, revolutionary statesman, and the founding father of the Republic of Turkey. He served as its first president and initiated rigorous modernization reforms.

name: Sr. S. Radhakrishnan
description: Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan was an eminent philosopher, scholar, and the second President of India. His birth anniversary on September 5th is celebrated nationwide as Teachers' Day.

name: Mohun Bagan Centenary
description: Commemorating the centenary of Mohun Bagan Athletic Club, established in 1889. It is one of the oldest football clubs in Asia and famously defeated the East Yorkshire Regiment in 1911 to win the IFA Shield.

name: Dr. P. Subbarayan
description: Dr. Paramasivan Subbarayan was an Indian politician, freedom fighter, and diplomat. He served as the Chief Minister of Madras Presidency and later as a Union Cabinet Minister in independent India.

name: Shyamji Krishna Varma
description: Shyamji Krishna Varma was a revolutionary freedom fighter, lawyer, and journalist. He founded the India House and the Indian Home Rule Society in London to promote the cause of Indian independence abroad.

name: Sayaji Rao Gaekwad III
description: Maharaja Sayajirao Gaekwad III was the progressive ruler of Baroda State who introduced free primary education, social reforms, and patronized arts and education. He was also a key patron of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.

name: Namakkal Kavignar
description: V. Ramalingam Pillai, popularly known as Namakkal Kavignar, was a patriotic Tamil poet, freedom fighter, and Gandhian. He wrote inspiring nationalist songs and was designated as the first Poet Laureate of Tamil Nadu.

name: 18th International Epilepsy Congress and XIV World Congress on Neurology
description: Commemorating the joint international medical congresses held in New Delhi in 1989. The event brought together global experts to discuss advancements in neurology and epilepsy research.

name: Pandita Ramabai
description: Pandita Ramabai Sarasvati was an eminent social reformer, educator, and pioneer in women's education and emancipation in India. She founded the Mukti Mission to support young widows and destitute women.

name: Pigeon Post
description: This stamp highlights the historical significance of the Pigeon Post, a traditional method of sending messages using homing pigeons. The Odisha Police Pigeon Service was one of the last active services of its kind in the world.

name: Acharya Narendra Deo
description: Acharya Narendra Deva was a leading theorist of the Congress Socialist Party, a prominent educationist, and a dedicated freedom fighter. He served as the Vice-Chancellor of Lucknow University and Banaras Hindu University.

name: Acharya Kripalani
description: Acharya Jivatram Bhagwandas Kripalani was an eminent Gandhian, freedom fighter, and politician. He served as the President of the Indian National Congress during the crucial transition of power in 1947.

name: Jawaharlal Nehru
description: Commemorating the birth centenary of Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru, the first Prime Minister of independent India. He was a key architect of the modern Indian nation and a champion of democratic socialism.

name: 8th Asian Track and Field Meet - Tracks of Friendship
description: Commemorating the 8th Asian Athletics Championships held in New Delhi in 1989. The event promoted sportsmanship, athletic excellence, and friendship among Asian nations.

name: Gurunath Bewoor
description: Sir Gurunath Venkatesh Bewoor was the first Indian Director-General of Posts and Telegraphs. He made significant contributions to the modernization and expansion of India's communication infrastructure.

name: Balkrishna Sharma Navin
description: Balkrishna Sharma "Navin" was a renowned Hindi poet, journalist, and freedom fighter. He made significant contributions to Hindi literature and served as a member of the Constituent Assembly of India.

name: Bombay Art Society
description: Celebrating the centenary of the Bombay Art Society, established in 1888. The society has been instrumental in promoting visual arts and providing a platform for Indian artists for over a century.

name: Likh Florican
description: Featuring the Likh Florican (Lesser Florican), an endangered bustard species endemic to the Indian subcontinent. The stamp highlights the urgent need for wildlife conservation and habitat protection.

name: A Hundred Year of Oil-Digboi Oilfield
description: Commemorating 100 years of the Digboi Oilfield in Assam, where Asia's first commercial oil well was drilled in 1889. This marked the birth of the modern petroleum industry in India.

name: Dr. M. G. Ramachandran
description: Maruthur Gopalan Ramachandran, popularly known as MGR, was an iconic Tamil actor, philanthropist, and politician. He served as the Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu and was posthumously awarded the Bharat Ratna.

name: Sukhna Shramdan, Chandigarh
description: Commemorating the massive voluntary public labor (Shramdan) initiative in 1989 to desilt and restore the ecological health of Sukhna Lake in Chandigarh. It remains a landmark event in community-led environmental conservation.

name: The Bombay Sappers Presentation of Colours
description: Commemorating the presentation of Regimental Colours to the Bombay Engineer Group, popularly known as the Bombay Sappers. They are a highly decorated engineering regiment of the Indian Army with a rich history of valor.

name: Asian Development Bank
description: Commemorates the 23rd Annual Meeting of the Board of Governors of the Asian Development Bank (ADB) held in New Delhi in 1990.

name: 150th Anniversary of First Postage Stamp
description: Issued to celebrate the 150th anniversary of the Penny Black, the world's first adhesive postage stamp, which revolutionized global communication.

name: Ho Chi Minh
description: Commemorates the birth centenary of Ho Chi Minh, the Vietnamese revolutionary leader and President who led his nation's struggle for independence.

name: Chaudhary Charan Singh
description: Honors the 5th Prime Minister of India, a champion of peasant rights and a prominent leader from Uttar Pradesh.

name: Indian Peace Keeping Force
description: Commemorates the return of the Indian Peace Keeping Force (IPKF) from Sri Lanka, recognizing their service and sacrifices during Operation Pawan.

name: Indian Council of Agricultural Research
description: Celebrates the contributions of the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) in promoting agricultural research and education in India.

name: Khudiram Bose
description: Honors the young Indian revolutionary Khudiram Bose, who was executed at the age of 18 for his role in the Muzaffarpur conspiracy against British rule.

name: Indo-Soviet Issue
description: A joint stamp issue between India and the Soviet Union, symbolizing the deep-rooted friendship and cultural ties between the two nations.

name: K. Kelappan
description: Honors K. Kelappan, popularly known as 'Kerala Gandhi', a prominent freedom fighter, social reformer, and journalist.

name: Care for the Girl Child
description: Issued to mark the SAARC Year of the Girl Child (1990), promoting awareness about gender equality and the rights of girls.

name: International Literacy Year
description: Commemorates the United Nations' International Literacy Year, emphasizing the global effort to eradicate illiteracy.

name: Safe Water
description: Highlights the importance of clean drinking water and sanitation for public health and sustainable development.

name: Pandit Sunderlal Sharma
description: Honors the social reformer and freedom fighter from Chhattisgarh, known for his efforts in the upliftment of marginalized communities.

name: XI Asian Games: Kabaddi
description: Commemorates the inclusion of Kabaddi as a competitive sport for the first time at the 11th Asian Games held in Beijing, China.

name: XI Asian Games: Racing
description: Celebrates the track and field events at the 11th Asian Games in Beijing, highlighting India's participation in athletics.

name: XI Asian Games: Cycling
description: Commemorates the cycling events at the 11th Asian Games in Beijing, showcasing the spirit of international sportsmanship.

name: XI Asian Games: Archery
description: Celebrates the sport of archery at the 11th Asian Games in Beijing, representing precision and focus.

name: A. K. Gopalan
description: Honors Ayillyath Kuttiari Gopalan, a prominent communist leader, freedom fighter, and the first Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha.

name: 3rd & 5th Battalion - the 5th Gorkha Rifles
description: Commemorates the centenary of the 3rd and 5th Battalions of the 5th Gorkha Rifles (Frontier Force) of the Indian Army.

name: Mahakavi Suryamall Mishran
description: Honors the 19th-century state poet of Bundi, Rajasthan, known for his patriotic and heroic poetry, particularly the epic 'Vansh Bhaskar'.

name: Children's Day
description: Issued on Children's Day, featuring a prize-winning painting by a child to celebrate the creativity and potential of India's youth.

name: Border Security Force
description: Commemorates the silver jubilee of the Border Security Force (BSF), India's primary border defense organization established in 1965.

name: Greetings
description: Part of a special greeting stamp series featuring floral designs, intended for use on festive and personal mail.

name: Greetings
description: Part of a special greeting stamp series featuring symbols of peace and goodwill, designed to add a personal touch to correspondence.

name: Cities of India: Bikaner
description: Celebrates the rich cultural heritage, architecture, and history of the desert city of Bikaner in Rajasthan.

name: Cities of India: Hyderabad
description: Commemorates the 400th anniversary of the historic city of Hyderabad, featuring its iconic monument, the Charminar.

name: Cities of India: Cuttack
description: Celebrates the millennium (1000 years) of the historic city of Cuttack in Odisha, known for its rich cultural legacy and silver filigree work.

name: Bhakta Kanakadas
description: Honors the 16th-century saint, poet, philosopher, and musician from Karnataka, renowned for his Haridasa compositions in Kannada.

name: Tercentenary of Calcutta: Shaheed Minar
description: Commemorates the 300th anniversary of the founding of Calcutta (now Kolkata), featuring the historic Shaheed Minar monument.

name: Tercentenary of Calcutta: Ganga - the River of Life
description: Celebrates the tercentenary of Calcutta, highlighting the Hooghly (Ganga) River's vital role in the city's trade, culture, and daily life.

name: Dnyaneshwari 1290-1990
description: Commemorates the 700th anniversary of the 'Dnyaneshwari', a commentary on the Bhagavad Gita written by the Marathi saint-poet Dnyaneshwar.

name: Banaras Hindu University
description: Commemorates the platinum jubilee of Banaras Hindu University (BHU), founded by Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya in 1916.

name: Road Safety
description: Issued to promote public awareness about traffic rules, safe driving practices, and the prevention of road accidents.

name: Seventh Triennale
description: Commemorates the 7th Triennale-India, an international exhibition of contemporary art organized by the Lalit Kala Akademi in New Delhi.

name: Jagannath Sunkersett
description: Honors the 19th-century philanthropist, educationist, and social reformer who played a pivotal role in the development of Bombay (Mumbai).

name: Tata Memorial Centre
description: Commemorates the golden jubilee of the Tata Memorial Centre in Mumbai, a premier institution for cancer treatment, research, and education.

name: Marine Mammals: River Dolphin
description: Highlights the conservation of the endangered Ganges River Dolphin, a freshwater mammal native to the Indian subcontinent.

name: Marine Mammals: Sea Cow
description: Promotes the conservation of the Dugong (commonly known as the Sea Cow), a vulnerable marine mammal found in India's coastal waters.

name: Beware of Drugs
description: Issued to raise global and national awareness about the dangers of drug abuse and illicit trafficking.

name: World Peace
description: Emphasizes India's commitment to global harmony, non-violence, and peaceful coexistence among nations.

name: Indian Remote Sensing Satellite - 1A
description: Commemorates the successful launch and operation of India's first indigenous remote sensing satellite, IRS-1A, which revolutionized resource survey and management.

name: Babu Jagjivan Ram
description: Honors the prominent Indian independence activist, social reformer, and statesman who served as the Deputy Prime Minister of India and championed the rights of the underprivileged.

name: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar
description: Commemorates the birth centenary of the chief architect of the Indian Constitution, social reformer, and champion of Dalit rights.

name: Tribal Dances: Valar
description: Depicts the traditional Valar dance, a ceremonial folk dance performed by the Garasia tribe of Rajasthan.

name: Tribal Dances: Kayang
description: Showcases the Kayang dance, a traditional folk dance performed by the Kinnauri tribe of Himachal Pradesh.

name: Tribal Dances: Hozagiri
description: Illustrates the Hozagiri dance, a traditional tribal dance of the Reang community of Tripura, known for its balancing acts.

name: Tribal Dances: Velakali
description: Features Velakali, a traditional martial dance of Kerala performed by the Nair community during temple festivals.

name: Ariyakudi Ramanuja Iyengar
description: Commemorates the legendary Carnatic music vocalist who established the modern 'Katcheri' (concert) format.

name: Karpoori Thakur
description: Honors the popular socialist leader and former Chief Minister of Bihar, affectionately known as 'Jan Nayak', who worked for the upliftment of backward classes.

name: Antarctic Treaty
description: Commemorates the 30th anniversary of the entry into force of the Antarctic Treaty, highlighting India's active participation in scientific research in Antarctica.

name: New Delhi-Diamond Jubilee
description: Celebrates the 60th anniversary (Diamond Jubilee) of the inauguration of New Delhi as the capital of modern India in 1931.

name: Sri Ram Sharma Acharya
description: Honors the spiritual leader, social reformer, and founder of the All World Gayatri Pariwar, who advocated for spiritual nationalism and social harmony.

name: K. Shankar Pillai - Cartoons
description: Commemorates Kesava Shankara Pillai, the father of political cartooning in India and founder of Shankar's Weekly and the Children's Book Trust.

name: K. Shankar Pillai - Cartoons
description: Honors the legendary Indian cartoonist K. Shankar Pillai, celebrating his immense contribution to political satire and children's literature in India.

name: Sriprakash
description: Honors the prominent Indian politician, freedom fighter, and administrator who served as India's first High Commissioner to Pakistan and Governor of several states.

name: Gopinath Bardoloi
description: Commemorates the eminent freedom fighter and the first Chief Minister of Assam, who played a pivotal role in preserving the territorial integrity of Assam during partition.

name: Rajiv Gandhi - A Life for India 1944-1991
description: Issued in memory of Rajiv Gandhi, the youngest Prime Minister of India, who championed modernization, technology, and youth empowerment before his tragic assassination in 1991.

name: Jain Muni Mishrimalji
description: Honors the revered Jain saint, scholar, and social reformer, known for his profound teachings on non-violence, self-discipline, and spiritual awakening.

name: Mahadevi Varma - Jayshankar Prasad
description: Commemorates two of the most celebrated Hindi poets and pillars of the Chhayavaad literary movement, Mahadevi Varma and Jaishankar Prasad.

name: 37th Commonwealth Parliamentary Conference
description: Commemorates the 37th Commonwealth Parliamentary Conference held in New Delhi, fostering democratic values and cooperation among Commonwealth nations.

name: Greetings
description: A special thematic stamp issued to convey festive greetings and goodwill, featuring traditional Indian decorative motifs.

name: Orchids: Cymbidium Aloifolium
description: Depicts Cymbidium aloifolium, an epiphytic orchid species native to India, highlighting the country's rich floral diversity.

name: Orchids: Paphioedilum Venustum
description: Features Paphiopedilum venustum, a rare and beautiful lady's slipper orchid species native to the eastern Himalayas.

name: Orchids: Aerides Crispum
description: Showcases Aerides crispum, a fragrant orchid species endemic to the Western Ghats of India.

name: Orchids: Cymbidium Bicolour
description: Illustrates Cymbidium bicolor, an attractive wild orchid species found in the southern and eastern regions of India.

name: Orchids: Vanda Spathulata
description: Features Vanda spathulata, a striking yellow-flowered orchid species native to South India and Sri Lanka.

name: Orchids: Cymbidium Devonianum
description: Depicts Cymbidium devonianum, a unique orchid species characterized by its dense, pendulous clusters of flowers, native to the Himalayas.

name: 2nd Battalion - the 3rd Gorkha Rifles
description: Commemorates the bicentenary of the 2nd Battalion of the 3rd Gorkha Rifles, honoring their valor, dedication, and distinguished service to the nation.

name: Kamaladevi Chattopadhyaya-Handicrafts
description: Honors the social reformer and freedom fighter Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay, celebrating her monumental efforts in reviving Indian handicrafts and handlooms.

name: Kamaladevi Chattopadhyaya-Puppet
description: Commemorates Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay's contribution to the preservation and promotion of traditional Indian puppetry and performing arts.

name: Chithira Tirunal Bala Rama Varma
description: Honors the last ruling Maharaja of the Kingdom of Travancore, known for his progressive social reforms, including the historic Temple Entry Proclamation.

name: 18 Cavalry
description: Commemorates the bicentenary of the 18 Cavalry, one of the oldest and most decorated armored regiments of the Indian Army.

name: Chidren's Day
description: Issued on Children's Day to celebrate the innocence and potential of children, featuring a prize-winning painting from the national design competition.

name: India Tourism Year 1991
description: Promotes India as a premier global travel destination during the designated 'India Tourism Year 1991', showcasing the country's rich cultural heritage.

name: International Conference on Youth Tourism
description: Commemorates the global conference held in New Delhi to promote youth travel, cultural exchange, and international understanding.

name: Nozart
description: Commemorates the bicentenary of the death of Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart, one of the most influential and prolific composers of the Classical era.

name: Saarc Year of Shelter
description: Commemorates the SAARC Year of Shelter, highlighting the regional commitment of South Asian nations to provide affordable and safe housing for all.

name: Run for Your Heart
description: Promotes cardiovascular health, physical fitness, and healthy living through the nationwide 'Run for Your Heart' public awareness campaign.

name: Asit Kumar Haldar
description: Honors the renowned painter of the Bengal School of Art and a close associate of Rabindranath Tagore, who made significant contributions to modern Indian art.

name: Yogasana: Bhujangasana
description: Depicts the Bhujangasana (Cobra Pose), highlighting the ancient Indian practice of Yoga for physical, mental, and spiritual well-being.

name: Yogasana: Dhanurasana
description: This stamp depicts Dhanurasana (Bow Pose), one of the primary postures in Hatha Yoga, highlighting India's ancient heritage of physical and mental well-being.

name: Yogasana: Ustrasana
description: This stamp features Ustrasana (Camel Pose), a backward-bending yoga posture known for improving posture, flexibility, and core strength.

name: Yogasana: Utthita Trikonasana
description: This stamp illustrates Utthita Trikonasana (Extended Triangle Pose), a foundational standing yoga posture that promotes balance and physical alignment.

name: YMCA - National Council of YMCA - Centenary
description: Commemorating the centenary of the National Council of YMCAs in India, which has played a significant role in youth development, community service, and sports since its establishment.

name: International Association for Bridge and Structural Engineering
description: Issued to mark the 14th Congress of the International Association for Bridge and Structural Engineering (IABSE) held in New Delhi, promoting global exchange in structural engineering.

name: V International Conference on Goats
description: Commemorating the 5th International Conference on Goats held in New Delhi, highlighting the importance of goat husbandry in rural economy and agriculture.

name: National Archives
description: Commemorating the centenary of the National Archives of India, the custodian of the non-current records of the Government of India and historical documents.

name: Krushna Chandra Gajapathi
description: Honoring Maharaja Krushna Chandra Gajapati, a key architect of modern Odisha, freedom fighter, and the first Prime Minister of the undivided Orissa Province.

name: Vijay Singh Pathik
description: Commemorating Vijay Singh Pathik, a prominent Indian revolutionary and peasant leader who led the famous Bijolia peasant movement in Rajasthan.

name: Adventure Sports: Hang Gliding
